detail.trap: Passive scrolling is not the same as deliberate practice. Regular experiments are the real threshold.
detail.rationale: Learning cadence is what separates occasional AI users from operators who compound gains over time.
detail.crosscheck: Learning should stay close to the respondent's fluency and workflow maturity.

prompt: How many AI agents are live in production with a named owner?

detail.trap: We use Copilot is Tier 1 on this question, not Tier 3. Copilot is assistive autocomplete, not an agent. Tier 3+ requires naming the agent and its owner.
detail.rationale: The single biggest gap in the live instrument. Named owner is the gate between Tier 2 and Tier 3 because an unowned agent is a liability, not an asset.
detail.crosscheck: Agent tier cannot exceed Tooling infrastructure tier (qs-c-p3) by more than 1.

prompt: What orchestrates your AI workflows?

detail.trap: Some Zapier flows often gets claimed as Tier 2 or 3. If nobody can be named as the owner of each flow, it is Tier 1.
detail.rationale: The plumbing underneath agents is what makes them compound or fail. Named owners at Tier 3 is non-negotiable.
detail.crosscheck: Orchestration should be within 1 tier of the agent question (qs-c-p3-agents). Agents without orchestration is a toy, orchestration without agents is waste.

prompt: How do you observe AI in production?

detail.trap: Tier 2 We log model calls is the most common overclaim. If nobody can open a dashboard and show cost per workflow, it is Tier 1.
detail.rationale: If you cannot see it, you cannot trust it. Tier 3 is the point at which AI becomes a first-class production system.
detail.crosscheck: Observability tier cannot exceed the Orchestration tier (c-p3-orchestration). You can only observe what you can orchestrate.

prompt: How are your agents connected to tools and data?

detail.trap: Custom API calls is Tier 2, not Tier 3. MCP or a shared registry is the gate. Without it, every agent reinvents the connection.
detail.rationale: Tool connection is where agent quality actually lives. MCP adoption at Tier 3 is the April 2026 benchmark for a serious implementation.
detail.crosscheck: Cannot exceed the agent tier (qs-c-p3-agents) by more than 1. Sophisticated connections on no agents is wasted infra.

prompt: How curated is the corpus your AI actually reads?

detail.trap: Putting docs in a vector store is Tier 1 or 2, not 3. Governance and ownership are what shift the tier.
detail.rationale: Most RAG implementations fail at the corpus, not the model. Named ownership is the step-change at Tier 3.
detail.crosscheck: Cannot exceed the Data Foundations score (qs-c-p2) by more than 1.

prompt: What does memory look like for your agents and workflows?

detail.trap: Vendor-provided memory features count as Tier 1 unless there is a deliberate architecture on top.
detail.rationale: Memory is the quiet differentiator. Most companies have not thought about it at all, which is Tier 0. Acknowledging the gap puts you at Tier 1.
detail.crosscheck: Memory tier cannot exceed Agents tier (qs-c-p3-agents). Memory for agents you do not have is not a real answer.

prompt: Where do your organisation’s best prompts actually live?

detail.trap: A big Notion library nobody has opened in a month is Tier 1, not Tier 2. Shared means actively referenced, not technically exists.
detail.rationale: Prompt storage reveals whether skills are treated as craft or disposable. The presence of version control at Tier 4 is the first serious sign.
detail.crosscheck: Cannot exceed Skills & Fluency median score (qs-c-p5) by more than 1. Sophisticated prompt storage without capable users is cargo culting.

prompt: How do you evaluate prompt and skill changes before deploying?

detail.trap: I ran it a few times and it seemed better is Tier 1, not Tier 3. A test set means written expectations, not gut feel.
detail.rationale: Most prompt improvements are vibes-based. An eval discipline is what separates teams shipping real craft from teams generating churn.
detail.crosscheck: Cannot exceed Observability tier (c-p3-observability) by more than 1. You cannot run evals you cannot observe.

prompt: Does this function have agents of its own, running day to day?

detail.trap: Built-in vendor AI features in a CRM, ATS or similar are Tier 1. Vendor features are not owned agents.
detail.rationale: Functions without agents are functions still paying full operational debt. Named ownership is the Tier 3 gate.
detail.crosscheck: Cannot exceed the company-level agent tier (qs-c-p3-agents) by more than 1.

prompt: How are prompts and skills shared across this function?

detail.trap: A Notion page of prompts from six months ago is Tier 1, not Tier 2. Active means in the last fortnight.
detail.rationale: Prompt reuse is the lead indicator of function-level craft. Solo use with no sharing is Tier 0, regardless of how sophisticated the individual is.
detail.crosscheck: Should not exceed the company-level prompts tier (c-p5-prompts) by more than 1.

prompt: Have you built any personal agents or automations that run without you triggering them?

detail.trap: ChatGPT scheduled tasks is Tier 2, not Tier 3. Multiple workflows is the gate.
detail.rationale: Builder density starts at the individual level. Someone who has shipped one personal automation is already Tier 2, which is more common than people admit.
detail.crosscheck: Personal agent tier cannot exceed the Individual skills tier (qs-i-p5) by more than 1.
